result:
Sign-up now follows ADR 0003, and all five reports are addressed. The full suite passes (74 files, 641 tests), and `tsc` and `eslint` are clean. I added `tests/services/auth-service.test.ts` for the new behaviour and left the existing tests alone.

- **Names (1, 5):** Sign-up derives the workspace slug up front, so a name never refuses it. `Admin`, `Billing`, `Support` and `Taskflow` get `admin-2` and so on. `J` and `山田` get `workspace`, suffixed if taken. `Al` gets `al`. The workspace name is capped at 64 characters by shortening the display name, so it always ends in `'s workspace` and the settings form accepts it. The cut never splits an emoji or other surrogate pair.
- **Addresses (2):** Addresses are stored lowercased and looked up case-insensitively, so sign-in, password reset and sign-up all treat `Alice@Example.com` and `alice@example.com` as one account. Old mixed-case rows are still found. Two existing accounts that differ only by case are not merged.
- **Duplicate addresses (4):** An existing address is refused as a `conflict` before anything is written. If two sign-ups for the same address race past the check, the loser gets the same `conflict` instead of a database error.
- **Throttling (3):** Sign-up spends one token from a new `auth:register` bucket (10 tokens, refilling 5 a minute) before anything is written. I picked those numbers; the ADR doesn't give any. A throttled sign-in, sign-up or password-reset confirmation now returns `rate_limited` (HTTP 429). A throttled password-reset request stays silent, including in its server action, which used to report an error. `RateLimitedError` moved into `src/lib/errors.ts` so services can throw it, and `action-errors.ts` still re-exports it.
- **Also fixed:** `uniqueSlug` could build an invalid slug when the 43-character cut ended on a hyphen, so it now strips that hyphen.

I left `docs/product/sign-up-notes.md` as is, since the README treats it as history.
